bibl.note: Main question 1 and all 30 source subquestions; all other units are excluded.

div.head: What is the chief end of man?
div.ab: Man's chief end is to glorify God, and enjoy him forever.

div.head: Is man a reasonable creature?
div.ab: Yes: For there is a spirit in man, and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth him understanding, Job 32:8.

div.head: Has he greater capacities than the brutes?
div.ab: Yes: God teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowls of heaven, Job 35:11.

div.head: Is man his own maker?
div.ab: No: It is God that hath made us, and not we ourselves, Psalm 100:3.

div.head: Is he then his own master?
div.ab: No: There is a Lord over us, Psalm 12:4.

div.head: Is he his own carver?
div.ab: No: Should it be according to thy mind, Job 34:33.

div.head: Is he his own end?
div.ab: No: For none of us lives to himself, or dies to himself, Romans 14:7.

div.head: Is it your business in the world to serve the flesh?
div.ab: No: For we are not debtors to the flesh, that we should live after the flesh, Rom. 8:12.

div.head: Is it to pursue the world?
div.ab: No: For we are not of the world, John 17:16.

div.head: Is your happiness bound up in the creature?
div.ab: No: For all is vanity and vexation of spirit, Eccl. 1:14.

div.head: Will the riches of the world make you happy?
div.ab: No: For a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth, Luke 12:15.

div.head: Will the praise and applause of men make you happy?
div.ab: No: For it is vain glory, Gal. 5:26.

div.head: Will sport and pleasure make you happy?
div.ab: No: For the wise man said of laughter, It is mad, and of mirth, What doth it? Eccl. 2:2.

div.head: Can the gain of the world make you happy?
div.ab: No, For what is a man profited, if he gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? Matthew 16:26.

div.head: Is God then your chief end?
div.ab: Yes, For of him, and through him, and to him are all things, Rom. 11:36.

div.head: Were you made for him?
div.ab: Yes: This people have I formed for myself, Isa. 43:21.

div.head: Were you redeemed for him?
div.ab: Yes: Ye are not your own, for ye are bought with a price, 1 Cor. 6:19,20.

div.head: Is it your chief business to glorify God?
div.ab: Yes: We must glorify God in our body and in our spirit, which are God's, I Cor. 6:20.

div.head: Must this be ultimately designed in all our actions?
div.ab: Yes: Do all to the glory of God, 1 Cor. 10:31.

div.head: Is God glorified by our praises?
div.ab: Yes: He that offers praise, glorifies me, Ps. 50:23.

div.head: And is he glorified by our works?
div.ab: Yes: Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit, John 15:8.

div.head: Is God your chief good?
div.ab: Yes: For happy is the people whose God is the Lord, Ps. 144:15.

div.head: Does all good come from him?
div.ab: Yes: For with him is the fountain of life, Ps. 36:9.

div.head: And is all good enjoyed in him?
div.ab: Yes: The Lord is the portion of my inheritance, and of my cup, Ps. 16:5.

div.head: Is it your chief happiness then to have God's favour?
div.ab: Yes: For in his favour is life, Ps. 30:5.

div.head: Is that the most desirable good?
div.ab: Yes: For his loving kindness is better than life, Ps. 63:3.

div.head: Do you desire it above any good?
div.ab: Yes: Lord, lift thou up the light of thy countenance upon us, Ps. 4:6,7.

div.head: And should you give all diligence to make it sure?
div.ab: Yes: Herein we labour, that whether present or absent, we may be accepted of the Lord, 2 Cor. 5:9.

div.head: Is communion with God in grace here the best pleasure?
div.ab: Yes: It is good for me to draw near to God, Ps. 73:28.

div.head: Is the vision and fruition of God in glory hereafter the best portion?
div.ab: Yes: For in his presence there is fulness of joy, Ps. 16:11.

div.head: Will you therefore set your heart upon this chief good?
div.ab: Yes: Lord, whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire besides thee; when my flesh and my heart fail, God is the strength of my heart and my portion for ever, Ps. 73:25,26.
